subject: MSA / Order Form redline: personal injury & tangible property carve-out (Harbor Retail)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Sarah Whitman <sarah.whitman@harborretail.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Harbor Order Form - personal injury / property damage carve-out (needs legal review)

Hi team,

Harbor's procurement sent back a redlined Order Form (attached) that adds an explicit carve-out: they want personal injury and tangible property damage excluded from the MSA/order-form liability cap. This is a non-standard ask for our SaaS terms and potentially exposes us to non-trivial risk.

Key points I pulled from their mark-up:
- Insert after Sec. 7.1: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, liability for personal injury or physical damage to tangible property arising from use of the Services shall not be subject to the limitations or caps in this Agreement."
- They also requested that Redwood be named as additional insured and that we accept a lower cap if insurance covers damages.

Can Legal weigh in on whether we can accept any form of this carve-out (and under what qualifier: negligence vs gross negligence vs willful misconduct)?

Commercial note for context: this is a late-stage procurement ask; deal team expects signature this month if we don't push too hard on this item. Dev — any commercial constraints/thresholds you want us to consider?

Attachments: Harbor_marked_orderform_20270301.pdf (customer redlines)

Thanks,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Michael Yu <michael.yu@harborlegal.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 11:37:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Harbor Order Form - personal injury / property damage carve-out (needs legal review)

Kimberly / Dev — thanks for flagging and for the redlines. I reviewed Harbor's proposed language and drafted an initial legal position (see attached). High level: we generally resist removing personal injury / physical property damage from our caps for a SaaS product absent very narrow circumstances (e.g., gross negligence or willful misconduct causing harm).

Recommended approach:
- Offer a compromise clause that carves out bodily injury and tangible property damage only where caused by Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence.
- Require customer to provide a certificate of insurance covering such risks and name Redwood as additional insured to the extent the claim relates to Harbor's premises/operations.
- Keep our primary monetary cap intact for all other claims.

Rationale: complete exemption for "personal injury / property damage" on a negligence standard would shift risk that is typically borne by customers or insurers and is inconsistent with our pricing and controls.

Attachments: legal_redline_MSA_section7_20270303.pdf (proposed MSA excerpt)

If Harbor pushes back on "gross negligence" we can consider a bridge where we accept "negligence" limited to a narrow factual carve-out (e.g., physical product shipped by Redwood or misconfigured on-prem agent) but I'd prefer to keep to gross/willful standard.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Whitman <sarah.whitman@harborretail.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 08:50:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Harbor Order Form - personal injury / property damage carve-out (needs legal review)

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Laura. Commercial considerations: Harbor is asking for a fairly material concession late in the process. Close plan and pressure:
- Procurement has said this redline is a gating item for signature this month.
- If we hold firm on gross negligence/willful misconduct the buyer warns they may escalate to procurement leadership and ask for higher discount/credits.

My ask to Legal: provide us with a short, customer-facing justification and a single alternative sentence we can offer in the counter (ideally one that mitigates risk but is simple enough for procurement to accept). Example one-liner: "Liability for personal injury or physical damage is only excluded from the cap where caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct; otherwise the cap in Section 7 applies."

If we must move further, what's the minimum cap number Legal can support if carves are removed? We can consider insurance-backed language (certificate + deductible threshold) if that helps.

- Dev

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Harbor Order Form - personal injury / property damage carve-out (needs legal review)

Thanks Laura — that is helpful. Based on the deal risk and Dev's note on timing, propose we send the following compromise to Harbor as our commercial/legal counter:

Proposed customer-facing language (for Order Form):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, liability for personal injury or physical damage to tangible property shall be excluded from the limitations and caps in this Agreement only to the extent such liability arises from Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence. In all other cases, the caps and limits in Section 7 shall apply. Customer shall provide, at Customer's expense, commercially reasonable insurance covering such risks and shall name Redwood as an additional insured to the extent permitted by the policy."

Why this works: it addresses Harbor's desire for a carve-out while preserving our commercial exposure limit except for the most extreme conduct. It also forces Harbor to involve its insurer, which is appropriate for tangible damage claims.

Please confirm if Legal can sign off on sending this language to Harbor. If yes, I'll have Sales send with a short note. Attachment: KPark_proposed_carveout_clause_20270305.txt (clean wording for the Order Form).

Thanks — want to keep momentum on this one.

Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Whitman <sarah.whitman@harborretail.com>

Cc: Michael Yu <michael.yu@harborlegal.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 09:02:11 -0700
Subject: Re: Harbor Order Form - personal injury / property damage carve-out (needs legal review)

Kimberly / Dev — thanks for the quick back-and-forth and for the proposed language. Harbor's legal team reviewed and we have a narrow request: Harbor cannot accept a "gross negligence / willful misconduct" threshold as the only path to recover for physical injury or property damage — procurement requires a negligence standard in our procurement templates. However, Harbor is willing to accept your insurer-first approach and provide the COI naming Redwood as additional insured.

If Redwood is comfortable with the COI + negligence standard (and a mutual release of consequential damages remains intact otherwise), we can finalize. Alternatively, Harbor is open to a short call tomorrow to align.

Attachment: Harbor_exec_commitment_20270309.pdf (internal procurement note).
